clue.text: Idea that's incomplete, however

indicators.note: something incomplete is missing a part, here its final letter

blocks.note: a thought is an idea

explanation.surface: Someone half-floats a notion and then hedges it with a qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words can open a contrasting remark, as in 'it was cold; however, we went out'.

clue.text: In South coast resort left substandard accommodation

blocks.note: Hove is a seaside town beside Brighton on England's south coast
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A seaside town is left with poor-quality lodgings for visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal, but it only links: the answer is in the resort plus left.
explanation.definitionFit: A hovel is a squalid, poorly built little dwelling, the kind of home nobody would choose.

clue.text: Frenchman, in single case, lacking refreshment

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
a case surrounds what it holds, so the word for single wraps round the name

blocks.note: a single person is not married
René is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: A Frenchman, alone in a court action, goes without a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not refreshed or revived has gone without being made new again, as a lapsed subscription.

clue.text: Gym equipment for runners in field

blocks.note: first meaning: vaulting apparatus in a gymnasium
second meaning: the competitors in a race, the field

explanation.surface: Apparatus at the gym is meant for athletes training outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: A field is all the starters in a race, so its runners are racehorses.
explanation.definitionFit: Gymnasts vault over padded boxes called this, and racehorses make up the field of a race meeting.

clue.text: Terrible weapon to fire at disorderly mob repeatedly

indicators.note: a disorderly crowd is out of its proper order, so its letters are rearranged
repeatedly says the shuffled group is used twice over, one copy after another

blocks.note: taken as written
the word mob rearranged
the same word rearranged again, the second time round

explanation.surface: Someone proposes using a dreadful weapon against an unruly crowd, again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear fission device is the archetypal devastating weapon, dropped or launched against a target.

clue.text: Relatively old form of religion?

blocks.note: surface reading: fairly ancient
setter's reading: a faith devoted to one's old relatives, those of earlier generations

explanation.surface: A question about a faith that dates back some way.
explanation.definitionFit: Veneration of dead forebears is among the oldest religious practices, found across China, Africa and elsewhere.

clue.text: Quaint archaism left in

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

blocks.note: an archaism is an old word
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An antiquated expression has been retained in a text.
explanation.definitionFit: Charming in an old-fashioned way, belonging to times past, like a village with thatched cottages.

clue.text: Half-heartedly shout downstairs

indicators.note: half the heart goes: one of the two central letters is dropped

blocks.note: to bellow is to shout

explanation.surface: Someone calls down the stairs without much enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: On a lower floor, or on a ship below decks, as in servants who lived downstairs.

clue.text: Among ordinary people, Dick is the entrepreneur

blocks.note: setter's reading: in the stock phrase for ordinary people, Tom, Dick and Harry, Dick is the one in the centre
surface reading: a man called Dick runs his own business

explanation.surface: Of all the common folk around, Dick is the one with the business sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrepreneur in its original sense is an intermediary trader standing between producer and customer.

clue.text: Importing staple food proved oddly expensive

indicators.note: to import is to bring something inside, so one piece goes into the other
done oddly means done strangely, out of the usual order

blocks.note: the word proved rearranged, split to take the food
rice is the staple food of much of the world

explanation.surface: Bringing in a basic foodstuff from abroad turned out to cost surprisingly much.
explanation.definitionFit: Something costing more than it is worth is dear, or expensive, in the sense of being priced too high.

clue.text: Game you reportedly found in old-fashioned case

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by sound
to fashion is to shape or make anew, so these letters are remade
something found in another is sitting inside it
a case surrounds its contents, so the remade letters go round the sound

blocks.note: the letter U is said exactly like the word you
the word old rearranged to make the case

explanation.surface: A board game is said to have turned up in an antique box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old-fashioned' reads as one adjective, but it splits: old is the fodder and fashioned the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a simple children's board game played with dice and counters, the British form of pachisi.

clue.text: Defoe's character as seen in part of Europe

blocks.note: first meaning: the surname of Daniel Defoe's heroine Moll
second meaning: the Dutch-speaking northern region of Belgium

explanation.surface: A literary figure is spotted on a trip abroad on the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Moll Flanders is the 1722 novel by Daniel Defoe, and the region lies in northern Belgium.

clue.text: One English novelist or another abridged

indicators.note: an abridged text is cut short, so the name loses its last letter

blocks.note: taken as written
H. G. Wells, another English novelist

explanation.surface: A choice between two English novelists, one of them in a shortened edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' points back to 'English novelist', so it stands for a second writer: Wells.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell, author of Nineteen Eighty-Four and Animal Farm, was an English writer of novels.

clue.text: Lighter domestic animal put on second

indicators.note: put on means placed after, so one piece follows the other

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a cow is a farm animal

explanation.surface: A farm animal is given a second helping, and comes out less heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' looks like a comparative of light, but it is a noun: a flat barge for unloading ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A scow is a flat-bottomed boat used, like a lighter, for carrying cargo to and from ships.

clue.text: Singularly useless product for the Japanese consumer

definitions.text: Singularly useless product for the Japanese consumer

blocks.note: surface reading: a remarkably pointless item sold in Japan
setter's reading: used singly, one alone is no good, since they work only in pairs
setter's reading: the consumer is someone eating

explanation.surface: A sneer at some pointless gadget marketed to Japanese shoppers.
explanation.definitionFit: Asian diners eat with a pair of thin sticks; a single one cannot pick up food.

clue.text: 18 in a state

blocks.note: first meaning: a good show, the answer to 18 across, here the Rodgers and Hammerstein musical
second meaning: one of the United States

explanation.walkthrough: The 18 answer, GOOD SHOW, is read literally: a hit stage musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma! is the celebrated Broadway musical, and Oklahoma is also a state of the American Midwest.

clue.text: Husband, somewhat expert, providing good living?

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
a bit means somewhat
able means skilled, expert

explanation.surface: A capable husband earns enough to give his family a comfortable life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good living' suggests income; the question mark flags that it means a place fit to live in.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitable building is fit for people to dwell in, suitable for occupation as a home.

clue.text: Church fitted us up within ecclesiastical garb

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards
within puts one piece inside another

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
fitted for a task means able to do it
taken as written

explanation.surface: The church has dressed us up in clerical robes.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasuble is the sleeveless outer vestment worn by a priest celebrating Mass.

clue.text: Merchandise with method? Well done!

blocks.note: goods are merchandise
the how of something is its method

explanation.surface: A salesman's pitch is followed by a cry of approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dated British exclamations of praise for something achieved, congratulating the person responsible.

clue.text: Spy chain

blocks.note: first meaning: James ..., Ian Fleming's secret agent 007
second meaning: a fetter or shackle, something that binds

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spy chain' suggests a ring of agents, which tempts RING; the crossing B from 16 kills it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleming's fictional agent is the archetypal spy, and bonds are fetters or chains that hold a prisoner.

clue.text: Aircraft, on time, coming to earth

blocks.note: a plane is an aircraft
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A plane landing on schedule touches down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming to earth' looks like landing, but earth is the definition, and one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is an example: the third world orbiting the sun in our solar system.

clue.text: Very large flower worshipped by ancient Egyptians

definitions.note: describes a god rather than naming one

blocks.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
the iris is a garden flower

explanation.surface: A huge bloom is revered by the people of the pharaohs.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris was the Egyptian god of the dead and the afterlife, a central deity of ancient worship.

clue.text: Staff joined by popular French master

indicators.note: joined by means followed on by, so the second piece comes after

blocks.note: a rod is a staff or stick
in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: Employees are joined by a well-liked French boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees, but it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin, sculptor of The Thinker, was a French artist regarded as a master of his craft.

clue.text: Corresponding part of some vital error reversed

indicators.note: part of tells us the answer is a stretch of the following words
reversed says the stretch is read backwards, right to left

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word to the start of the last

explanation.surface: A section of some critical mistake has been undone.
explanation.definitionFit: Relative and corresponding both describe things considered in proportion or comparison to each other.

clue.text: Prolific scorer's off-drive

indicators.note: something off is out of true, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the word drive rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricket batsman who scores lots of runs plays a shot to the off side.
explanation.walkthrough: An off-drive is a cricket stroke; a scorer here is a writer of musical scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi composed some twenty-eight operas, making him a prolific writer of musical scores.

clue.text: A number of Germans were dishonest

blocks.note: first meaning: a German song, a number in the musical sense
second meaning: told untruths

explanation.surface: Some German people did not tell the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a quantity but means a song; Germans here is the possessive sense, numbers by Germans.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lied is a German art song, like those of Schubert, and lied is the past tense of lie.

clue.text: Where those who serve drinks are placed inside

definitions.text: Where those who serve drinks are placed

blocks.clueFragment: Where those who serve drinks are placed
blocks.note: first meaning, taken literally: the station of barmen and barmaids at the counter
second meaning: inside is slang for in prison

explanation.walkthrough: 'Serve' hints at serving time, which fits the prison sense of the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the idiom for imprisoned, and bar staff literally stand back of the counter they pour at.

clue.text: Type that's trapped in ooze that's shallow

indicators.note: something trapped in another is held inside it

blocks.note: a kind is a type
to seep is to ooze

explanation.surface: Some kind of creature is stuck in a thin layer of mud.
explanation.definitionFit: Superficial, only on the surface, as in the saying that beauty is only that far down.

clue.text: The short form of 23's argument

indicators.note: a short form is a clipped version of a longer word

blocks.note: taken as written
the answer to 23 across is a relative, and a sister is one

explanation.surface: A summary of some earlier answer's case, in abbreviated form.
explanation.walkthrough: SIS is the familiar short form of sister.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is a proposition put forward and defended, the line of reasoning in a debate or paper.
